title: Mobile app accessibility
description: For an iOS or Android app: screen reader labels, larger text, touch target size and accessibility checks in UI tests.

sources.title: Apple, scaling fonts automatically with Dynamic Type
Android Developers, make apps more accessible
Android Developers, test your app's accessibility

rules.instruction: Give each changed control and meaningful image an accessibility label (`accessibilityLabel` on iOS, `contentDescription` on Android) that says its purpose, and mark decorative images as hidden.
rules.verification: Complete the changed flow with VoiceOver and with TalkBack, and record any element announced without a purpose.

rules.instruction: Use text styles that follow the system text size setting, and let layouts grow so text stays readable at the largest sizes.
rules.verification: Run the changed screens at the largest text size on both platforms and check for truncated, overlapping or clipped text.

rules.instruction: Give each tappable element a target of at least 44 by 44 points on iOS and 48 by 48 dp on Android, with spacing between adjacent targets.
rules.verification: Run Xcode's Accessibility Inspector audit and Android's Accessibility Scanner on the changed screens and fix target size findings.

rules.instruction: Add an accessibility check to the UI tests of changed screens: `performAccessibilityAudit` in XCUITest, and checks built on the Compose testing APIs or the Accessibility Test Framework on Android.
rules.verification: Run the UI test suites in CI and confirm the accessibility checks execute on the changed screens.
